chunks.content: # [Master Express Lesson 8] Special Topic on Clothing Detail Presentation: Ultra-Realistic 3D Detail Rendering for Clothing This document covers advanced techniques and procedures for clothing detail presentation using CLOUD software, including sticker tools, reflective materials, metal and silk effects, trims, buttons, nails, buckles, and custom components. It focuses on technical workflows, rendering settings, and practical tips for ultra-realistic 3D clothing detail creation. --- ## Addressing Common Questions from Previous Sessions This section provides solutions for common technical questions related to using CLOUD software tools for clothing design, including filling slides, rendering reflective materials, creating metal silk effects, and handling fabric hairline cutouts. ### Filling Slides with Stickers - Open the project file in CLOUD. - Use either 2D or 3D sticker tools to add PNG format stickers directly. - To fill an area with a sticker: - Select the PNG sticker tool. - Right-click and choose the "repeat version" option to fill the entire area. - Copy and paste stickers across different versions to replicate fills. ### Displaying Reflective Materials - Open the garment file (e.g., a skirt). - Select the shiny property to add a gloss effect. - Adjust reflection properties: - Lower roughness increases brightness. - Higher reflection intensity brightens the surface. - Typically, reflective effects are localized: - Use a highlight map (black-and-white image) to control reflection areas. - Black parts reflect; white parts do not (or invert for opposite effect). - Adjust reflection intensity and brightness for desired visual effects. ### Showing Gold and Silver Silk Effects - Add a PNG sticker containing silk textures (not purely white but with white silk patterns). - Change the sticker type to "metal" to simulate strong surface reflection. - Adjust transparency and increase roughness to reduce reflection intensity. - This method produces realistic gold and silver silk appearances. - Film effects will be discussed separately. ### Handling Simulation Pictures Behind Buttons and Fabric Hairline Cutouts - Simulation pictures behind buttons may become invisible; this is a known issue reported to development. - To identify fabric hairline cutouts in the drawing room window: - Hairline cutouts are blue and hard to distinguish visually. - Use the name of the hairline cutout to identify it—changing fabric and cutout names to Chinese can simplify recognition. - Alternatively, remove hairline cutouts manually and use automatically generated ones for speed. --- ## Creating Trims: Film Effects and Procedures This section explains how to create ultra-realistic trims, particularly film effects, using Photoshop and CLOUD software, focusing on procedural steps and rendering adjustments. ### Making Film Trims in Photoshop (PS) 1. chunks.content: ### Making Film Trims in Photoshop (PS) 1. Open Photoshop and create a blank canvas. 2. Add a new layer and use the oval selection tool while holding Shift to draw a perfect circle. 3. Fill the circle with a gradient color (metal often has a white spot in the middle). - Adjust the size of the white area for realism. 4. On the background layer, draw an oval with a gap in the middle to simulate the beam gap. 5. Return to the circle layer and delete the middle part to create a cut. 6. Shrink and adjust the circle to fit the beam size. 7. Create a double sequence (left and right side). 8. Save the file in PNG format with names like "obvious" for clear beam visibility. 9. Create additional superimposed lines following a similar process. ### Importing and Using Film Textures in CLOUD - Open CLOUD and create a new project. - Import the PNG film trims as textures. - Change texture type to metal for reflective properties. - Adjust the rendering interface to check the beam effects. - For internal line patterns, make them slightly wavy and add multiple beam layers linearly. - Use shortcut keys to adjust texture frame positioning, direction, and size. - Connect axes if necessary to align UV mapping. - Refresh rendering to observe the light effect linearly. --- ## Creating Self-Defined Buttons in CLOUD Plugin This section details the creation of custom buttons, including shape design, OBJ export, and application along garment lines. ### Designing Buttons - Draw a circle with a smaller diameter for smoother edges. - Center the button board on the cross for successful creation. - Adjust thickness and contact surface to ensure button touches the garment surface. - Use inner circles to create holes by right-clicking and selecting "convert to hole." - Modify curve rates to define corner sharpness. - Add texture if desired. - Export the button as an OBJ file, naming it clearly for easy identification. ### Importing and Applying Buttons - Open a project file and create multiple versions (e.g., "nico1"). - Use single or multiple target options when importing OBJ: - Single target applies fabric to one object version. - Multiple targets apply the same fabric to multiple object versions. - Select thin or thick versions depending on desired mesh detail. - Use the glue tool to merge points and avoid seam line disconnections. - Adjust axis orientation and UV coordinates to maintain texture integrity. - Save with text files to preserve map paths and metal data. ### Adding Buttons Along Internal Lines - Select the button tool and pick the custom OBJ button. - Add buttons along internal lines like a "tree wheel" pattern. - Adjust button size progressively from one side to another. - Copy and paste buttons to create size variation. - Change button type to metal for reflective appearance or plastic for less intense reflection.

Add buttons along internal lines like a "tree wheel" pattern. - Adjust button size progressively from one side to another. - Copy and paste buttons to create size variation. - Change button type to metal for reflective appearance or plastic for less intense reflection. ### Advanced Button Adjustments - Add small rectangles and adjust positions to refine button shapes. - Delete textures or adjust edge curves as needed. - Use the hook tool (new in version 5.2) to add buttons along panel outlines automatically. - Apply new fabrics and sew panels with proper sewing types. - Modify buttonhole line length for closer fit to buttons. - Note: Maximum number of buttons per line may be limited (e.g., max 42 buttons). --- ## Creating Additional Clothing Details: Nails, Buckles, and Balls This section explains the creation of nails, 8-word buckles, and spherical objects for clothing using CLOUD tools. ### Creating Nails - Draw a circle at the bottom and adjust it to fit the internal line. - Copy and arrange multiple nails in 3D for convenience. - For self-locking nails, place them centered on the cross. - Adjust top and bottom parts, grinding and resizing as needed. - Use sewing functions to attach nails with correct cylinder radius (~80-89mm) and line length (~125mm). - Add fixed needles and simulate for proper attachment. - Harden fabric and adjust model positions to avoid gaps. - Use hairpin stickers on sides to smooth gaps. - Import nails as OBJ with multiple targets to apply different fabrics on parts. - Adjust sizes and apply metal material for realistic finish. ### Creating 8-Word Buckles - Draw and convert curves into circles with rounded corners. - Create hollow inner line borders. - Adjust buckle width (e.g., 37.5mm) and strap size accordingly. - Add patterns on straps for design consistency. - Freeze buckle and place strap over it. - Use project file to save buckle with pattern for easy reuse. - Change buckle type to metal, adjusting visibility. ### Creating Spherical Objects (Balls) - Use the round tool to draw a sphere with radius 50. - Adjust particle diameter (e.g., 1) for smooth edges. - Set rendering thickness and speed for size control. - Shrink size using corner controls with Shift and mouse keys. - Export as OBJ for further use. - Use math formulas to calculate axis lengths, considering right-angle triangles and curves. - Approximate lengths by dividing by √2 (~1.4) or 2π (6.28) as needed. --- ## Additional Tips and Notes ### Software and Workflow Efficiency - Utilize shortcut keys extensively in CLOUD and Photoshop for speed. - Naming conventions and organized file saving help manage multiple components. - Pay attention to axis orientation and UV coordinates when importing/exporting OBJ files.
